routes.label: Subtract the union of the small semicircles

question:
Three semicircles of radius \(1\) are constructed on diameter \(\overline{AB}\) of a semicircle of radius \(2.\) The centers of the small semicircles divide \(\overline{AB}\) into four line segments of equal length, as shown. What is the area of the shaded region that lies within the large semicircle but outside the smaller semicircles?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_12B_Q16_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The small semicircles overlap, so we must account for those overlaps before subtracting their area. Name their centers \(U,O,V\), in order from \(A\) to \(B\). Since \(AB=4\), the four equal segments each have length \(1\), and \(O\) is also the large semicircle's center. Each small semicircle lies inside the large one: its center is at most \(1\) from \(O\), and the triangle inequality places every point within another \(1\) of that center at distance at most \(2\) from \(O\).

Consider the overlap of the semicircles centered at \(U\) and \(O\), and call their intersection above \(AB\) point \(T\). The lengths \(UT,OT,UO\) all equal \(1\), so \(UOT\) is equilateral and its angles are \(60^\circ\). Its altitude bisects the unit base, giving height
\[
\sqrt{1-\left(\frac12\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Thus its area is \(\sqrt3/4\).

Drawing \(UT\) and \(OT\) splits the overlap into this triangle and two circular segments. Each segment is a \(60^\circ\) unit sector with the triangle removed. Consequently, the overlap area is
\[
L=2\left(\frac{60}{360}\pi\right)-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}
=\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}.
\]
The other adjacent pair has the same overlap. The outer two semicircles meet only at \(O\), so there is no other overlap of positive area. Adding the three small areas counts each adjacent overlap twice; subtracting one copy of each gives their union's area.

The large semicircle has area \(2\pi\), and each small semicircle has area \(\pi/2\). Therefore the shaded area is
\[
2\pi-\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}-2L\right)
=\frac{7\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{7\pi}{6}-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
